what: Tenet Healthcare runs hospitals and, through its majority-owned United Surgical Partners, a large network of ambulatory surgery centres where procedures are done without an overnight stay.
customers: Patients and the insurers and government programmes that pay for their care, plus physicians who operate in its facilities.
money: acute care hospitals, mostly in Texas, Florida and California
moat: Surgery centres jointly owned with the surgeons who use them, which aligns incentives and makes the physicians unlikely to take cases elsewhere.
risks: Hospital reimbursement from government programmes is politically determined
Uninsured patients rise if health insurance subsidies expire
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 16% with a 16% operating margin
Procedures keep shifting from hospitals to lower-cost surgery centres, which is its best business
Selling hospitals to fund surgery centre expansion has improved the mix
watch: Ambulatory segment case growth and hospital admissions.
